subject: Aurora Health: evidence & routing checklist for SCCs / UK addendum / TIA
messages:
From: Marta Lopez <marta.lopez@aurorahealth.com>

Cc: legalops@aurorahealth.com

Subject: Redwood DPA + SCC/TIA evidence — initial ask

Hi Grace / Redwood team,

Thanks again for the call this morning. Procurement and Legal at Aurora have requested a concise evidence package so our internal reviewers can confirm:
- SCC mapping from each processing flow to the appropriate module (specifically: generation, embeddings, and audit logs)
- Any UK IDTA / UK addendum evidence for data residency and subprocessors
- The TIA/DTIA scoping note (what controls we rely on for transit and at-rest safeguards)

Can you send a single ZIP with a short index (one page) plus the artifacts? Target timeline from our side is COB Tuesday 2026-05-25 so we can feed it to our InfoSec council. If there are items that require an NDA or a secure share, tell us the preferred channel (DocuSign NDA / secure bucket).

Also, please call out any subprocessor changes or planned onshore caching fallback options — Aurora is especially sensitive to any multi-hop processors in the EU/UK -> US path.

Appreciate the quick turnaround.

— Marta Lopez
Head of Procurement, Aurora Health
M: +44 7700 000000

Attachment: aurora-evidence-request-20260520.pdf (pdf stub)

From: grace_oconnor@redwood.example.com

Subject: Re: Redwood DPA + SCC/TIA evidence — initial ask

Hi Marta — thanks for the clear list. Looping in Kimberly (Security), Laura (Legal operations) and Jonas (Infra) to pull the package. High-level plan:

1) Quick index page (1 pager) that maps artifacts to your request (we'll include this as redwood-evidence-index.pdf).
2) SCC mapping spreadsheet that shows which processing step uses which SCC module and where KEK/KMS boundaries are (redwood-scc-mapping.xlsx).
3) TIA scoping note: short doc describing controls relied upon for transit (TLS+mutual auth), at-rest encryption, and our cache residency/TTL rules (TIA-scoping.md).
4) UK addendum / IDTA evidence: excerpted certs and the signed UK addendum template where applicable; if Aurora needs the full UK addendum executed we'll provide the DocuSign link and proposed signing cadence.
5) Technical artifacts: KMS architecture diagram, key rotation schedule, and a short note on the onshore cache fallback behavior.

Kimberly / Jonas / Laura — can you confirm what we can publish to a shared Drive vs what needs a secure share? Also flag any subprocessor updates (we should include the current subprocessor CSV).

Marta — we'll aim to deliver an initial package by EOD Monday (2026-05-24) and a finalized ZIP by your COB Tuesday deadline. If you prefer a 30-minute walkthrough once you've reviewed the package, we can schedule next week.

Best,
Grace O'Connor
Director, Customer Security & Trust
Redwood Inference

Attachment: redwood-evidence-index.pdf (pdf stub)

From: kimberly_park@redwood.example.com

Subject: Re: Redwood DPA + SCC/TIA evidence — evidence inventory and redlines

Grace / team — quick status and asks:

Inventory I'm attaching:
- kms-keystore-architecture.pdf (architecture diagram & KMS responsibilities)
- redwood-scc-mapping.xlsx (SCC mapping per flow)
- onshore-cache-fallback-notes.txt (behavioral note and thresholds)
- subprocessor-current.csv (CSV export of processors and regions)

Publish guidance:
- Public share (Drive link) OK: redwood-scc-mapping.xlsx, onshore-cache-fallback-notes.txt, subprocessor-current.csv
- Secure share required (restricted link / NDA): kms-keystore-architecture.pdf (contains key-handling detail).

Technical notes to call out for Aurora:
- For generation/streaming we apply continuous batching and prefix KV caching. The cache TTL is 5 minutes by default; onshore fallback (EU outage) will route to onshore cache in the UK regional pool — this is logged and visible in audit exports. See onshore-cache-fallback-notes.txt.
- We use envelope encryption with per-tenant DEKs stored in a KMS; master key rotation occurs quarterly (see kms-keystore-architecture.pdf).
- Network transit uses mTLS + AES-256. For cross-border routing we can pin to EU-only serving nodes for your account under a Dedicated or Private deployment if Aurora requires full EU residency for processing.

Laura — legal will prepare the redlined UK addendum for signature. Jonas, can you confirm if the infra team needs any special proc for the DocuSign-executed UK addendum before enabling dedicated routing?

I will produce the secure Drive share for KMS artifacts and send the DocuSign signing link once legal confirms the addendum version.

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Senior Security Engineer
Redwood Inference

Attachments: kms-keystore-architecture.pdf (secure stub), subprocessor-current.csv (csv stub)

From: Marta Lopez <marta.lopez@aurorahealth.com>

Cc: procurement@aurorahealth.com, legalops@aurorahealth.com, kimberly_park@redwood.example.com, laura_bennett@redwood.example.com

Subject: Re: Redwood DPA + SCC/TIA evidence — initial ask

Grace / Kimberly / Laura — thank you, this looks good and pragmatic.

Couple of clarifications from Aurora InfoSec:
- The council will accept a secure Drive link for the KMS diagram but will require a short statement confirming whether Redwood acts as sole custodian of the master KEK or if any subprocessor has custodial access.
- On the routing: if you can state the exact failover sequence (EU pool -> UK regional pool -> onshore fallback), that will help our ops team sign off. The onshore fallback note you attached is useful; please add a simple flow graph to the index page.
- Finally, please include the proposed DocuSign timeline for executing the UK addendum (we'd prefer a 48-hour signing window once redlines are agreed).

We'd like the ZIP by Monday EOD as discussed. After review, we'll book a 30-minute sync next Tuesday 2026-05-26 10:00 UK time to walk the artifacts and any open redlines.

Thanks again — Marta
